title: The NRI's Guide to World Cup 2026 at MetLife Stadium, New York
excerpt: Match schedule, desi eats from Oak Tree Road to Jackson Heights, transit tips, and everything Indian Americans need to know about attending the World Cup Final in the tri-state area.
body:
The World Cup Final is in your backyard. MetLife Stadium — officially "New York New Jersey Stadium" for the tournament — hosts 8 matches including the biggest game in football on July 19. For the massive NRI community across New Jersey and New York, this is a once-in-a-generation opportunity.

## Match Schedule

| Date | Match | Kickoff (ET) |
|------|-------|-------------|
| Sat, Jun 13 | Brazil vs Morocco | 6:00 PM |
| Tue, Jun 16 | France vs Senegal | 3:00 PM |
| Mon, Jun 22 | Norway vs Senegal | 8:00 PM |
| Thu, Jun 25 | Ecuador vs Germany | 4:00 PM |
| Sat, Jun 27 | England vs Panama | 5:00 PM |
| Tue, Jun 30 | Round of 32 (TBD) | TBD |
| Sun, Jul 5 | Round of 16 (TBD) | TBD |
| **Sat, Jul 19** | **FIFA World Cup Final** | **3:00 PM** |

## Where to Eat: Desi Food Near MetLife

The tri-state area is NRI heaven when it comes to food. Here are your best bets:

**Closest to the Stadium:** Sanjha Dhaba (850 Paterson Ave, East Rutherford) is just 2 miles away — authentic Punjabi dhaba-style with Patiala Goat Curry and fresh tandoori breads.

**Jersey City (10 miles):** Laree Adda on Grove Street is the move — nihari, samosas, and Kashmiri chai until 1 AM. Sapthagiri Taste of India on Newark Ave has the best Butter Masala Dosa, and Brick Lane Curry House stays open until 2 AM on weekends with a full bar.

**Oak Tree Road, Edison/Iselin (35 miles):** This is the real deal — the largest South Asian commercial district in America with 400+ businesses. Moghul Restaurant has been an institution for 20+ years. Bikanervala for chole bhature and raj kachori. Desi Galaxy food court for budget-friendly chili paneer and vada pav. Chatkaz has a perfect 4.9-star rating for their pure veg thalis.

**Jackson Heights, Queens (12 miles):** NYC's original Little India. Angel earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand for its goat dum biryani. Kabab King runs 7 AM to 2 AM daily. Maharaja Sweets is a must for mithai.

## Getting There: Transit Is Mandatory

**There is no spectator parking at MetLife Stadium.** All attendees must use public transit or shuttles.

**NJ Transit Train + Bus Shuttle ($98 round-trip):** This is the primary option. Trains depart from New York Penn Station to Secaucus Junction, then dedicated shuttles run to the stadium. Only 40,000 transit tickets per match day — book early via the NJ Transit mobile app. Important: 4 hours before kickoff, Secaucus Junction and Penn Station are restricted to World Cup ticket holders only.

**Charter Shuttle ($20 round-trip):** Pickup from Port Authority Bus Terminal and Midtown East. Purchase through the NYNJ Host Committee website.

**Rideshare:** Allowed but drops off at the Meadowlands Racetrack, not the stadium. Expect extreme surge pricing post-match.

**Parking:** American Dream Mall has limited premium spots at $225 (advance only). Final day parking is already sold out.

## Where to Stay

**Secaucus, NJ (3 miles):** Best transit access. Budget-friendly chains along the NJ Turnpike with direct NJ Transit to the stadium.

**Jersey City (10 miles):** The smart NRI play — huge Indian community, tons of restaurants on Newark Ave, PATH train to Manhattan, many World Cup Airbnbs available.

**Edison/Iselin (35 miles):** Heart of Indian NJ. Oak Tree Road is Little India. Dozens of restaurants, grocery stores, and temples. Requires a car or long NJ Transit ride.

## Desi Community Spots

**BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham** in Robbinsville is a must-visit — the largest Hindu temple in the Western Hemisphere with stunning Carrara marble and Shayona Cafe for vegetarian food. The iconic Ganesh Temple in Flushing, Queens has been serving the community since 1977.

For Indian groceries, **Patel Brothers** has locations across NJ and has everything you need. The cluster of stores on Oak Tree Road is the most comprehensive South Asian shopping destination in the US.

## Tickets

Tickets are available at [FIFA.com/tickets](https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/tickets) on a first-come, first-served basis. The FIFA resale marketplace is also live for eligible ticket holders. Avoid third-party sites — the FBI has warned about dozens of spoofed FIFA websites.

**Pro tip:** Brazil vs Morocco (Jun 13) and the World Cup Final (Jul 19) will be the hottest tickets in America this summer. If you can get them, don't hesitate.
author: Diaspora Desk
